sections.h2: What does the Jefferson County Clerk do when a house sells?
sections.html:
The Jefferson County Clerk's Legal Records Division is the official repository for deeds, mortgages, releases and liens on Louisville real estate. A sale is not on the public record until the deed has been accepted, taxed and indexed there.

The clerk's website lists the Deed Room at Metro Hall, 527 W. Jefferson St., Room 204, Louisville, KY 40202, telephone 502-574-6220. Wills and name changes also pass through that room once the probate court has approved them, which matters if the home came to you through an estate. Delinquent property tax is handled in a separate window at 527 W. Jefferson St., Suite 100a.

The office also offers ClerkAlert, a free notice service that tells owners when a document is filed under their name. Sellers who held a house for years sometimes sign up after closing so a surprise lien or forged deed cannot sit unnoticed.

sections.h2: What does the Clerk charge to record a deed in Jefferson County?
sections.html:
A plain deed costs $50 to record in Jefferson County, and a mortgage costs $80. The clerk publishes the full schedule under KRS 64.012 as amended by Senate Bill 114, and the figures below come from that page.

Selected Jefferson County Clerk recording fees (source: Jefferson County Clerk, Document Fees)
DocumentRecording fee
Deed$50
Deed with a release$96
Deed with a vendor's lien$50
Mortgage$80
Mortgage with assignment$126
Release of a deed or mortgage$46
Affidavit of descent$50
Will$50

Charges can climb past the base figure in a few ways:

  • Instruments sent by mail carry an extra $1 for postage starting September 1, 2026.
  • A certified copy runs $5 for the first three pages and 50 cents for each page after that.
  • Another $4 applies for each extra book or reference added to a document.
  • Notary service inside the clerk's office is $2 per signature.

sections.h2: How is the Kentucky transfer tax figured on a Jefferson County deed?
sections.html:
The grantor, which means the seller, owes 50 cents for every $500 of value or fraction of $500 stated in the deed. KRS 142.050 sets that rate, and the clerk computes it and collects it before the deed can be recorded.

On Jefferson County's Census median home value of $248,400, the value divides into 497 units of $500 once the fraction is counted, so the tax comes to $248.50. Ask the title company to show that line on the settlement statement so it is not confused with the recording fee.

The statute lists transfers that owe nothing. Those most likely to matter to a seller are:

  • A transfer between spouses, or between former spouses in a divorce.
  • A deed given only to secure or release a debt.
  • A deed that confirms or corrects one already recorded.
  • A transfer under foreclosure, or a voluntary surrender in lieu of foreclosure.
  • A parent to child or grandparent to grandchild transfer for nominal consideration.

When one of these applies, the Clerk's recording rules say the deed must cite the statute that explains why the tax is not due.

sections.h2: What must a deed contain before the Jefferson County Clerk will accept it?
sections.html:
A deed has to meet the Clerk's formatting and content checklist or it is rejected at the counter. The list follows the national PRIA formatting standards that the Kentucky County Clerks Association adopted for 2020 filings.

  • Paper of 8.5 by 11 inches preferred, white, printed on one side, with no staples, seals or highlighter marks.
  • Ten-point Times New Roman or similar type, black ink preferred, and a three-inch top margin on page one for the recorder.
  • A preparation statement with the preparer's name, address and signature. A line reading "Drafted by" does not satisfy it.
  • Complete addresses for grantor and grantee, plus the mailing address for the tax bill.
  • A property description, the source of title by deed or will book and page, and the fair market value.
  • Notary signature and notary ID number, with the names of the grantor and grantee in the acknowledgment.
  • An original or certified copy, with the correct fee and a signed check.

Deeds for a company, LLC or partnership are accepted only after the entity is on file with the Secretary of State. A seller who is an LLC should confirm that filing before closing day.

sections.h2: How do mortgage releases work for a Jefferson County sale?
sections.html:
The payoff lender releases its lien, and the release is recorded for $46 once the loan is satisfied. Where the deed and a release are filed together, the Clerk's schedule shows $96 for the pair.

The Clerk's guidance says a Kentucky mortgage is recorded in the county where the land lies, under KRS 382.110. It binds third parties from the time it is acknowledged and recorded under KRS 382.080. A release therefore needs the book and page of the mortgage it clears, and your closing agent will pull that reference from the title search.

Ask the lender for a payoff letter good through the closing date, then confirm with the title company that the release was sent for recording. An unreleased mortgage on the Jefferson County record can slow the buyer's own financing later.

sections.h2: What happens at the Clerk when Jefferson County property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid current-year bills move from the Sheriff to the County Clerk at the close of business on April 15, and the clerk then holds them as certificates of delinquency. The Sheriff's schedule shows a 10 percent penalty and a 10 percent Sheriff's add-on fee by then, and the clerk's stage adds interest of 1 percent per month plus fees.

The County Attorney's page says the full set of added fees, interest and penalties comes to roughly 40 percent of the bill once a certificate exists, and that the certificate then carries interest of 12 percent a year. The Clerk holds a tax lien sale each summer, and any bill that does not sell can still be bought through the year. A certificate that a third party buys can carry that buyer's own costs.

Payments on an unsold certificate go to the Clerk at 527 W. Jefferson St., Room 100. The County Attorney's page says personal checks and phone payments are not taken there, and that certified checks, cashier's checks and money orders work by mail. Anyone who cannot pay in full can ask the County Attorney's Tax Division about a payment plan, and a bill on a plan cannot be sold at the tax sale.

For a seller, the practical step is to order a payoff figure from the Clerk before listing, so the buyer's title company can pay it from proceeds.

sections.h2: What is Jefferson County, Kentucky, like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Jefferson County is Kentucky's largest county, and since the 2003 city-county merger its borders match those of Louisville, the county seat. The Ohio River forms the northern edge, and the county covers 380.8 square miles of land. Incorporated places such as Jeffersontown, St. Matthews and Middletown kept their own governments inside Louisville Metro.

Two school systems serve the county: Jefferson County Public Schools, and the Anchorage Independent district, which runs kindergarten through eighth grade. Census QuickFacts supplies these figures:

  • 2025 population estimate: 795,222, up 1.6 percent from the 2020 base.
  • Housing units in 2025: 366,702.
  • Owner-occupied rate, 2020 to 2024: 62.1 percent.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $248,400.
  • Median gross rent: $1,149.
  • Median household income: $69,866.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 3,001.

The Jefferson County PVA counts 83 incorporated taxing jurisdictions among its roughly 60,000 properties in smaller home rule cities. Sellers there should check whether the city sends a separate tax bill, since the clerk's recording step is the same everywhere in the county.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Jefferson County house?
faqs.a: Record it with the Jefferson County Clerk's Legal Records Division, whose Deed Room is at Metro Hall, 527 W. Jefferson St., Room 204, Louisville, KY 40202, phone 502-574-6220. Title companies usually file for the buyer at closing, and the Clerk also accepts electronic filings through approved vendors.

faqs.q: How much is the recording fee for a deed in Jefferson County?
faqs.a: A deed is $50, and a deed filed with a release is $96. A mailed instrument adds $1 for postage starting September 1, 2026. The transfer tax of 50 cents per $500 of value is collected separately.

faqs.q: Who pays the Kentucky transfer tax on a sale?
faqs.a: The seller does, because KRS 142.050 puts the tax on the grantor named in the deed. The clerk collects it before recording. Exempt transfers, such as those between spouses or in foreclosure, owe nothing if the deed cites the exemption.

faqs.q: Can the Clerk reject my deed?
faqs.a: Yes. A deed is rejected if it lacks a preparation statement, a source of title, the fair market value, a tax bill mailing address, a proper notary block or the correct fee. An LLC grantor must also be on file with the Secretary of State first.

faqs.q: What if I owe back property tax on the house?
faqs.a: Pay it through the Sheriff before April 15, or through the County Clerk after the bill becomes a certificate of delinquency. Request a payoff amount before you list the house so the figure is ready for the title company. The County Attorney's office handles payment plans for delinquent bills.
